clusters.text: Texans should not vote for James Talarico.
Ken Paxton is a criminal.
James Talarico has said there are six genders.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The 2021 committee remarks that Talarico's critics cite were about sexes, not genders. 
He said "modern science recognizes that there are many more than two biological sexes – in fact, there are six."
 
The Texas Tribune describes this as referring to people with chromosomal variations.
 LGBTQ Nation's fact check rated the "six genders" wording Half True because 
he said there are six sexes, referring to intersex chromosome variations, not six genders.
 Later he told Fox News, 
"There are not six sexes. There are two."
 Several outlets and partisan sources paraphrase the remark as "six genders" (TIME, The Federalist, the RNC chair). I found no record of him using the word "genders" with the number six. The claim swaps "genders" for "sexes", so it misstates what he said, even though he did argue that sex and gender are not binary.

clusters.text: James Talarico is too radical for Texas and must be defeated.
The story that James Talarico was treated at Lindner Center of Hope or a mental health facility is false.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The Lindner Center of Hope publicly stated on Oct. 11 that 
"Representative James Talarico has never received treatment from Lindner Center of Hope."
 Talarico posted that 
"I've never even been to Ohio"
. He also told the Dallas Morning News editorial board he was 
not absent for mental health care and was home in bed with the flu
. The rumor rested on an unverified audio recording of a call that influencers Nick Sortor and Rhein Amacher posted. Snopes found the claimed discharge timing 
didn't match Talarico's schedule
. It also reviewed visual evidence, which it did not publish, 
that Talarico was at his Austin home every day of his flu
. Snopes, PolitiFact and FactCheck.org each rated or answered the claim as false or "No." One caveat is that the facility told the Daily Wire it 
does not confirm or deny whether any individual is or has been a patient
. That is a general policy line and sits alongside its specific public denial. The wider "or a mental health facility" wording can't be disproved in absolute terms. Still, no credible evidence supports it, and the fact-checkers' findings and the timeline point against it.

clusters.text: James Talarico thinks tax dollars should pay for sex changes for kids.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The claim rests on Talarico's 2023 vote against SB 14, which banned gender-transition treatments for minors and barred public funding for them. 
The Dallas Morning News spot check says he did vote against the bill, but a no vote doesn't by itself show he supported taxpayer-funded surgeries for minors.
 
PolitiFact (via the Houston Chronicle) found no evidence that he backed any legislation using taxpayer money for gender-reassignment surgery
, and it rated a near-identical ad claim False. 
CNN reports that he also voted for failed amendments that would have limited the ban to surgeries while leaving hormone therapy and puberty blockers allowed
. 
FactCheck.org reports that his campaign says he opposes gender-reassignment surgery for minors, and that he told Fox News he would "absolutely" support a national ban on such surgery for minors.
 The claim turns a vote against a broad bill into an affirmative position on "sex changes for kids" paid for with taxpayer money, and the records don't show that position.

clusters.text: James Talarico said 'God is non-binary.'
clusters.verdict_basis:
The quote is accurate. Snopes rated it "Correct Attribution." 
It reports that Talarico made the statement on Oct. 14, 2021, while speaking against Texas bill HB 25, a youth sports bill.
 FactCheck.org confirms this: 
Talarico said "God is nonbinary" during his Oct. 14, 2021 Texas House floor remarks against HB 25.
 Fox News reports the fuller wording as 
"God is both masculine and feminine and everything in between. God is non-binary."
 Talarico has also acknowledged saying it. He 
called it "provocative"
 and said he 
was trying to say that human categories can't define God
. The claim has no date and doesn't say he has since walked it back, but it is worded only as an attribution of what he said, and that holds up. FactCheck.org noted that Paxton's ad omitted context about the remark. That bears on how the ad framed the quote, not on whether he said it.

clusters.text: James Talarico was in a mental health facility, the Lindner Center, during his absence.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The claim is contradicted by the evidence. 
The Lindner Center posted on social media that Talarico "has never received treatment from Lindner Center of Hope."
 Talarico 
reshared that post and wrote that he has "never even been to Ohio."
 The claim traces back to an influencer's audio recording of a phone call. 
The Texas Tribune reports that Rhein Amacher said he called the center posing as Talarico's cousin and made up a patient code.
 PolitiFact found that the call's timeline 
conflicts with Talarico's public appearances on Oct. 9 and Oct. 10
, and rated it Pants on Fire. The AP also reported that 
images it reviewed showed Talarico at home over several days
. Snopes, FactCheck.org and the Dallas Morning News also rated the claim false. Talarico says he was at home with the flu. Reporting notes that the Lindner Center says it does not confirm or deny patients, but it did issue an explicit denial about Talarico.

clusters.text: James Talarico lied when he said he had the flu.
clusters.verdict_basis:
I found no record or reporting showing that Talarico lied about having the flu.
- Talarico said on Sept. 30 that 
he went to urgent care in Dallas and was diagnosed with the flu
. CNN reported this, and the Texas Tribune reported that 
his campaign said he was off the trail because of the flu
.
- CBS News reported that the campaign shared security-camera footage that 
appears to show Talarico at his home in Texas for the first eight days of October
. That is consistent with his being sick at home.
- The main alternative story was that he was being treated at Ohio's Lindner Center of Hope. The Center said 
Talarico "has never received treatment from Lindner Center of Hope"
, and the Texas Tribune/KERA called the story 
debunked
.
- The one wrinkle is that Talarico later said he saw his primary care physician. Gateway Pundit called this 
a changed story
. CBS noted that 
he later told a reporter he went to his primary care physician
. That is a detail about which doctor he saw, and it doesn't show the flu was invented.
- Paxton and Trump publicly doubted the flu explanation, but I found no medical records or other evidence contradicting it. There is also no independent medical confir

clusters.text: Ken Paxton was impeached by his own party.
clusters.verdict_basis:
On May 27, 2023, the Texas House impeached Paxton 121-23. 
Speaker Dade Phelan and 59 other Republicans joined 61 Democrats, and all 23 "no" votes came from Republicans.
 That makes 60 Republicans in favor. The impeachment began with a 
Republican-led House General Investigating Committee
, which 
voted unanimously to send the articles to the full House
. So the House did impeach him, and Republican-led bodies and many Republican members drove it. But the claim leaves out several things. The vote was bipartisan, and Democrats supplied about half of the "yes" votes. Most Republicans who voted did vote yes, but a sizable minority voted no, so it was not a unified party action. The claim also omits that 
the GOP-controlled state Senate acquitted him on all 16 articles tried
, with 
only two Republicans voting to remove him on any count
 (CBS News). The core fact, that Republican House members impeached a Republican, is accurate. "By his own party" overstates it by implying a party-wide act, and it ignores the acquittal.

clusters.text: A Lindner Center of Hope employee or psychiatric hospital said James Talarico was recently discharged.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The claim comes from an Oct. 11 X post by Nick Sortor and Rhein Amacher. It included an audio recording of a woman who said she was at the Lindner Center of Hope and that Talarico was just discharged. 
Amacher wrote that the caller identified herself as a female facility employee and said Talarico had been discharged within the previous 24–48 hours.
 Nobody has verified the caller's identity or role. 
The Lindner Center itself said that evening that Talarico "has never received treatment" there.
 
Talarico told the Dallas Morning News editorial board he was at home with the flu.
 The hospital did not say he was discharged. It said the opposite. Fact-checkers found no credible evidence for the claim. 
Snopes said it reviewed visual evidence, which it did not publish for privacy reasons, that Talarico was at his Austin home every day of his illness.
 Snopes rated the claim False. 
PolitiFact rated the related claim that the audio proves a discharge on Oct. 10 "Pants on Fire."
 
FactCheck.org also answered "No" and said the center rebutted the rumors.
 The only support is an unauthenticated recording, which the facility and the candidate both contradict.

clusters.text: James Talarico said parents who do not transition their kids are abusive.
clusters.verdict_basis: The 2019 hearing on HB 1910 is the source of the claim. Fox News and others report that Talarico, speaking on that bill, said denying a child's gender identity is "incredibly harmful" and that "whether or not we label it with the term abuse, it's abusive for sure." The bill would have barred courts from weighing a parent's refusal to acknowledge a child's gender identity in custody cases. That is not the same as saying parents "who do not transition their kids" are abusive. The comment concerned refusing to acknowledge or affirm gender identity, and the reports I found do not show him mentioning medical or social transition. He also hedged on the legal label, saying he opposed ruling it out as abuse. His campaign says he supports parental rights, and a Texas PAC ad claiming he backs jailing such parents was found unsupported by his legislative record. The claim is therefore a compressed, overstated version of a real quote. It also leaves out that the quote is from 2019. Reporting also notes he voted against the 2025 bill (HB 1106) that excluded refusal to affirm from the legal definition of abuse. Paxton's wording adds that Talarico thinks parents should have kids taken away, which

clusters.text: James Talarico said his favorite drag queen is Alyssa Edwards.
clusters.verdict_basis:
Fox News published video of a man asking Talarico at a campaign event, "Who's your favorite drag queen in Texas?" 
Talarico answered, "Oh, my gosh. Probably Alyssa Edwards."
 The Washington Examiner, Townhall, Western Journal and PinkNews reported the same exchange. 
PinkNews says Paxton posted about it on X on 14 September.
 Talarico's campaign spokesperson did not dispute the exchange. 
The spokesperson responded by attacking Paxton instead.
 Two small caveats: the question asked about Texas drag queens, and Talarico said "probably". Neither changes the substance of the claim. I did not find an independent record of where or when the video was filmed. 
Western Journal says it is unclear where the footage was taken.

clusters.text: James Talarico thinks parents who do not transition their kids should have their kids taken away.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The claim matches Ken Paxton's own post of Sept. 14, 2026, which adds that Talarico called such parents "abusive". It comes from a resurfaced 2019 House committee clip on HB 1910. That bill would have barred courts from weighing a parent's history of acknowledging or declining to acknowledge a child's gender identity when deciding custody. According to 
Fox-reported coverage, Talarico said some people consider an unwillingness to acknowledge a child's gender identity "abusive and destructive"
. According to 
RedState's account, he said "whether or not we label it with the term abuse, it's abusive for sure"
. 
The bill did not pass.
 Even the friendly PJ Media write-up concedes that 
he did not explicitly say authorities should classify this as abuse warranting removal of children
.

The sources I found show he opposed a bill that would have kept this kind of evidence out of custody decisions, and that he called refusing to acknowledge a child's gender identity abusive. None of them shows him saying, or clearly implying, that parents who decline to "transition" a child should have the child taken away. The claim also turns "not acknowledging gender identity" into "not transitioning"

clusters.text: James Talarico is ahead of Ken Paxton in the polls.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The claim has no numbers or dates, so it holds if Talarico leads in polls generally. He does, though mostly by small margins. The RealClearPolling table (polls from Sept. 18 to Oct. 11) has an 
average of Talarico +3
, and 
47–45 in Marist, 51–45 in NYT/Siena and 50–44 in YouGov
. Polls close to the date the claim was posted also show him ahead. Marist (Sept. 17–20) had 
Talarico 50%, Paxton 44% among registered voters
. NBC5/Telemundo had 
46% to 43%, within the margin of error
, and Texas Southern had 
47% to 46%
.

The lead is not uniform. Fox 7's tracker describes the race as 
a statistical tie
. Emerson's earlier poll had 
Paxton 47%, Talarico 46%
. In RealClearPolling's list, 
Quantus Insights and UMass Lowell show ties
. "Ahead in the polls" is accurate as a summary of the polling average and most individual polls, but many leads are within the margin of error, so it doesn't mean a decisive lead.

clusters.text: If the unverified claims about James Talarico's whereabouts are true, his campaign will likely end.
James Talarico would surrender the border to the cartels.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The claim is a rhetorical characterization, not a checkable fact. The record doesn't support "surrender the border to the cartels," although Talarico's record gives Paxton room to attack it. Talarico has a published border plan, which the Texas Tribune says includes 
more Border Patrol agents and surveillance technology to detect illegal crossings
. He also wants 
better resources at official ports of entry to detect illegal drugs
. Fox 4 reports that he 
voted against SB 4 and HB 7, which created a state border protection unit
, and Fox News reports he once 
called to slash Texas' entire border-security budget
. PolitiFact rated a related Paxton ad "Mostly False" because it 
left out Talarico's "lock on the door" remark
. The claim ignores his stated support for border security measures, and I found no record of him proposing to cede control of the border to cartels.

clusters.text: James Talarico said only the child can determine a child's gender identity.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The Daily Wire reviewed a Texas House Juvenile Justice and Family Issues Committee hearing. 
It reports Talarico said, "There's only one person who can determine a child's gender identity, and that's the child."
 Breitbart repeats the same quote (
"only one person who can determine a child's gender identity, and that's the child"
). Both are partisan outlets, and I found no primary transcript or neutral news report that reproduces the line. Neutral coverage of the same 2019 hearing on HB 1910 (Fox via Yahoo, Hannity's transcript, and PolitiFact's summary of the ad) quotes only his "abusive" remarks about denying a child's gender identity. The Daily Wire's account has Talarico clarifying that 
"I don't think gender identity is something people can see differently,"
 which means the sentence was part of a longer exchange whose context I couldn't see. The paraphrase "only the child can determine a child's gender identity" matches the reported wording and is probably accurate. It rests on one outlet's account of the video, and I couldn't confirm it against the hearing record. The claim also leaves out the date (2019) and the setting (a debate over custody and child-abuse law).

clusters.text: Texans are tired of 30 years of Republican control and want change.
Ken Paxton has declined the debate invitations that James Talarico accepted.
clusters.verdict_basis:
Reporting consistently says Paxton has not accepted any of the invitations Talarico accepted, but it generally doesn't say he formally declined them. Talarico accepted invitations from Hearst/NBC-Telemundo, WFAA/TEGNA, Nexstar/KXAN and CNN. 
The Hearst/Telemundo deadline passed with Paxton's team neither accepting nor declining.
 On CNN, 
a Paxton senior adviser criticized the proposed debate but did not say whether Paxton would participate.
 
WFAA reported that Paxton's campaign had not responded to messages since Aug. 24.
 
KVUE reported Paxton has not accepted any invitation for an on-stage face-off,
 and 
his campaign said in July, "of course we are going to debate James Talarico."
 Paxton has since said 
he and Talarico could not agree on details
. The Dallas Morning News did describe him as 
"declining invitations to debate"
, and the Texas Democratic Party and Talarico's campaign call it a refusal. The claim is accurate that Paxton hasn't taken up the offers. But "declined" overstates the record, which shows non-acceptance, silence and criticism of one host (CNN) rather than a formal refusal.

clusters.text: Ken Paxton lunged at a tourist to snatch his phone after being filmed with his mistress in London.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The claim states as fact something that is only an allegation. The Daily Mail reported an anonymous American tourist's account, which Mediaite, the Daily Beast and Yahoo relayed. The tourist said he filmed Paxton with Tracy Duhon on Westminster Bridge on July 1, and that Paxton then confronted him and lunged twice for his phone ([Mediaite](https://www.mediaite.com/politics/ken-paxton-accused-of-lunging-at-tourist-who-filmed-him-with-mistress/); [Yahoo](https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/articles/ken-paxton-accused-lunging-tourist-012935493.html)). The coverage consistently uses "accused" and "allegedly." The tourist is unnamed and told London's Metropolitan Police but did not pursue charges. 
Paxton's campaign did not respond to the allegations.
 I found no police record, no video of the confrontation itself, and no response from Paxton. The wife reportedly filmed part of it, but I found no published footage. The Daily Mail reports that Paxton and Duhon have never denied the affair ([Texas Democrats' repost of the Daily Mail](https://www.texasdemocrats.org/post/ken-paxton-accused-of-attacking-couple-who-filmed-him-with-mistress-reported-to-london-police)). That repost is a partisan sour

clusters.text: Texas taxpayers paid $6 million in fines and lawsuits over Ken Paxton's bribery.
clusters.verdict_basis: The $6 million figure comes from the $6.6 million judgment in the whistleblower case. The Texas Tribune and WFAA report that in April 2025 a Travis County judge found Paxton's office violated the Texas Whistleblower Act by firing aides who reported him to the FBI. Paxton dropped his appeal in July 2025. The aides had alleged bribery and abuse of office tied to Nate Paul. The judgment was for retaliation, though, not for bribery, and it was not a fine. The Texas Senate acquitted Paxton on the impeachment articles, which included bribery. I found no bribery conviction. One tracking site, The Paxton Record, says it found no public confirmation as of Sept. 29, 2026 that the Legislature had appropriated the money or that it had been paid. The wording "paid" and "fines and lawsuits over bribery" therefore overstates the record. The claim looks like a paraphrase of a Ron White remark on Rogan, and it is a rounded-down, loosely worded version of the $6.6M judgment. A Courier Texas tally puts total taxpayer costs above $12 million by adding impeachment trial costs and outside counsel, but that is a different figure and is not what the claim says.

clusters.text: Alyssa Edwards has described himself as a drag performer who works with children.
clusters.verdict_basis:
Edwards's Sept. 23, 2026 open letter to Paxton does contain both self-descriptions, but she kept them separate. 
She wrote that she is "an educator of 30 years, a choreographer, an entrepreneur, a mentor – and yes, I also happen to be a drag performer."
 
She also named Beyond Belief Dance Company as what she is most proud of, a program where "generations of young people" have been encouraged to discover their creativity.
 Her children-related work is dance education, and she never described it as part of her drag work. The claim's wording runs the two together, which can suggest drag aimed at children. Reporting (Dallas Morning News, TheWrap, Advocate) says Paxton's ad used clips of her teaching dance students, and 
the Advocate says Edwards criticized a video that portrayed her as a threat to children
. The claim is also worded "himself," while 
the Dallas Morning News and other outlets refer to Edwards as "her."

clusters.text: James Talarico's campaign has stopped actively planning events in the final stretch of the race.
clusters.verdict_basis: Talarico did stop appearing in person for about 12 days. CNN and NBC News reported that his last in-person Texas event was Sept. 26. The Dallas Morning News reported that at least two events were scrapped: an Oct. 5 event for Black voters and an Oct. 6 Austin fundraiser. The campaign said the cause was the flu. It said he had held 100+ public events and would return soon. His calendar showed no candidate appearances, only canvassing, phone banks and get-out-the-vote gatherings (Townhall, Hot Air). The claim goes further than this. It says the campaign "stopped actively planning events in the final stretch." But the campaign kept scheduling field events. It also kept a CNN/Jubilee town hall set for Oct. 14. By Oct. 14, CNN reported he had returned to public events over the weekend, including Austin City Limits. The records back a temporary illness-related pause in his in-person appearances and some cancellations. They don't back a campaign-wide halt to event planning, so the claim as worded is misleading.

clusters.text: Texans should vote for Ken Paxton.
Mental health treatment would disqualify James Talarico from serving as a Texas senator.
Ken Paxton is corrupt.
Ken Paxton is a coward for avoiding a debate.
Karl Rove explains in a Wall Street Journal opinion piece why he is voting for a Texas Democrat.
clusters.verdict_basis:
Karl Rove did publish a Wall Street Journal opinion piece on Sept. 16, 2026, titled "Why I'm Voting for a Texas Democrat." 
In it he confirmed he would vote for Jon Rosenthal, the Democrat running for Texas Railroad Commissioner, over Republican Bo French.
 
Wonderwall's report dates the op-ed to Sept. 16.
 The Sept. 16 date matches the day the claim first appeared on X. The claim fits the op-ed's title and subject: a WSJ piece explaining why he is voting for a Texas Democrat. The claim does not name the Democrat, and the Senate race context could lead readers to assume it is Talarico. Townhall noted that 
he is not voting for James Talarico
. The Texas Tribune reported that 
Rove did not say whether he'd vote for Paxton.
 As worded, the claim is accurate, but it could mislead anyone who reads it as being about the Senate race.

clusters.text: James Talarico disappeared from the campaign trail for nine days in early October.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The Texas Tribune, AP, NBC DFW and Houston Public Media all describe a nine-day absence from the trail, ending with his Oct. 9 Austin City Limits appearance. 
AP says Republicans highlighted his absence from Oct. 1 to Oct. 9.
 That matches "nine days in early October." The count is contested, though. 
CNN counted 12 days, from his last public appearance on Sept. 26.
 
Talarico's campaign said he joined a Sept. 30 Zoom, which makes the absence closer to nine days.
 "Disappeared" is Paxton-side framing. 
Talarico and his campaign said he was home in Austin with the flu, and the New York Times reviewed time-stamped home-security images that showed him there from Oct. 1 to Oct. 8.
 FactCheck.org also found that online rumors of mental-health treatment in Ohio were false. The nine-day, early-October absence from in-person campaigning is accurate. The word "disappeared" suggests an unexplained absence, and the reporting doesn't support that.

clusters.text: James Talarico believes there are six genders and voted to let men play girls' sports.
clusters.verdict_basis:
In a 2021 House debate on a transgender-athlete bill, Talarico said 
"Modern science recognizes that there are many more than two biological sexes — in fact, there are six."
 That was a statement about biological sex, not gender. 
NPR describes it as a reference to six chromosomal variations, and Talarico told CBS "I know there are two sexes, men and women."
 He does not appear to have used the phrase "six genders" in that remark, and he now says he believes there are two sexes. The "six genders" wording is Paxton's and Republican shorthand. On sports, the records show he 
voted against House Bill 25 in 2021, which tied public-school athletes' teams to the sex recorded at or near birth
. The Daily Signal also reports that he helped defeat SB 29. Voting against a restriction is not the same as voting to let men play girls' sports. Talarico said he opposed the bills as 
"overly broad"
 and backed narrowing amendments. In September 2026 he said he 
opposes trans athletes playing in girls' sports "if it risks safety or fairness"
 (
19th News
, Texas Tribune). The claim therefore rests on a real quote and a real "no" vote, but it recasts "six biological sexes" as "six genders" and a "no

clusters.text: James Talarico offered to debate Ken Paxton on Fox News.
clusters.verdict_basis: On Sept. 24, 2026, Talarico challenged Paxton to a Fox News debate moderated by Bret Baier. He made the challenge on stage at the Texas Tribune Festival. The Texas Tribune reported it, and so did CBS Austin, The Washington Post and MS NOW. His own quoted words were "Let's do Bret Baier on Fox News." The next day his campaign posted a voicemail video repeating the offer (HuffPost). Fox News later said it would host a debate if both candidates committed (Houston Chronicle, Washington Post), and Paxton had not accepted any debate as of mid-October (KXAN, The Hill). One caveat: the offer is dated Sept. 24, and the claim was first seen on X on Sept. 9. If it was posted on Sept. 9, it came before the offer, and I found no earlier Fox-specific offer. The claim as worded is accurate today. Whether it was accurate on the day it was posted is a separate question.

clusters.text: James Talarico wants amnesty for all illegal immigrants.
clusters.verdict_basis:
Talarico does support a pathway to citizenship for some people who are in the country illegally. On Fox News he said it should go to those "who have been here for years and decades" and don't pose a public-safety threat. He said it should require paying back taxes, learning English and passing a criminal background check, and he rejected the idea that anyone without a criminal record should simply be allowed to stay (
Washington Examiner
; 
Yahoo/Fox transcript
). The Dallas Morning News and a New Republic piece describe the same conditional, comprehensive-reform approach, paired with border security and ICE prioritizing dangerous criminals. The New Republic notes it is 
not the large-scale amnesty that Senate Democrats passed in 2013
. "Amnesty for all illegal immigrants" is a partisan label that overstates a position limited to long-term, law-abiding residents who meet conditions. The "mass amnesty" wording appears mainly in conservative outlets such as Twitchy and Hot Air. I found no Talarico statement or plan calling for unconditional legalization of everyone.

clusters.text: James Talarico challenged Ken Paxton to a debate 85 days ago and Paxton has not responded.
clusters.verdict_basis:
Talarico did use the "85 days" figure himself. 
He posted on X, "I challenged Ken Paxton to a debate 85 days ago, but no one has heard from him."
 He repeated it to NBC DFW. 
Reporting says he publicly challenged Paxton in July to three televised debates
, which roughly fits the timeframe. Reporting also supports that Paxton has agreed to no debate. 
As of Oct. 9, none was scheduled, and Paxton had not publicly responded to Trump's call for one (AP/PBS).


The flat statement that Paxton "has not responded" overstates the record. 
AP reports Paxton's campaign said in July that he would debate, later objected to some proposed moderators, and suggested an agreement with an outlet was imminent, though none was announced.
 
The Washington Post likewise reports the campaign initially said it would debate so long as the moderators were neutral.
 
Talarico himself says Paxton's campaign declined three invitations from Texas TV stations.
 That is a response, even if it is not an acceptance. After the claim appeared, 
Paxton was asked about a debate on Fox News and said "We've been working on that for months with him."
 Talarico's campaign disputes that account. Paxton's non-acceptance is we

clusters.text: Ken Paxton should agree to debate James Talarico.
In a private Zoom with Austin Sierra Club activists, James Talarico said capitalism is an oppressive system he wants to dismantle.
clusters.verdict_basis:
CNN's KFile reported that Talarico, then a 31-year-old state representative, 
described capitalism as an "oppressive system" during a Sierra Club event, grouping it with White supremacy and climate change
. He said that understanding how the three systems work together was necessary to begin 
"dismantling them."
 The event was 
a virtual climate candidate forum from September 2020
. It was 
hosted by the Austin chapter of the Sierra Club and featured four other Texas House candidates
. The quote and the Austin Sierra Club setting are accurate. Two parts of the wording are shaky:
   - "Private": CNN's own summary calls it a candidate forum. Only secondary outlets such as 
National Review, citing a recording obtained by CNN's KFile
, call it a "private Zoom meeting". The claim's wording matches the Paxton-aligned PAC's post.
   - No date: The claim leaves out that this was six years ago, in 2020. Talarico 
said on Oct. 14 that he was referring to "crony capitalism" that disproportionately benefits the wealthy
, and his campaign calls him a "proud capitalist".

   The claim is built on a real quote, but the "private" framing is not established by CNN and the missing date and context m

clusters.text: James Talarico switched his 'beat meat' campaign to 'eat meat' because it hurt his image.
clusters.verdict_basis:
The claim copies a line from Trump's Sept. 9 speech at the Republican midterm convention in Dallas, not from anything Talarico said or did. 
HuffPost reports that Talarico doesn't seem to have used "beat meat" as a campaign slogan.
 The record shows something narrower. In a 2022 Texas House fundraiser speech, 
Talarico called for reducing meat consumption and said his reelection campaign had become a "non-meat campaign." He did not say he is a vegan.
 I found no "beat meat" campaign and no "eat meat" rebrand. 
PolitiFact's Oct. 13 check says Talarico has repeatedly said he eats meat.
 
His campaign has posted photos of him eating meat at the Texas State Fair and at Fiesta San Antonio.
 
In a March interview he denied "all accusations of veganism."
 The "bad for his image" motive is only Trump's characterization. The claim also doesn't say Trump made the statement, and its first-seen date of Sept. 10 is the day after the speech.

clusters.text: James Talarico's flu explanation for his absence is not believable.
James Talarico opposes trans athletes in girls' sports if it endangers safety or fairness.
clusters.verdict_basis:
